body:
## Batch 3 - Startup & Rebind Perf (master plan)

Kills the measured felt slowness from perf.log: triple/2N+1 rebinds on launch, per-rebind GUI-thread stat storms and sqlite commits, and the 8.4s file-browser expand stall.

### Commits
- **B3.1** Collection restore + tab ops down to one rebind each. Every `_add_project_tab` (and close/detach) was running TWO full rebinds - the unblocked `setCurrentIndex` fired `_on_proj_tab_changed -> _switch_to_slot` and then the explicit `_switch_to_slot` ran again. Collection restore paid 2N+1 rebinds for N projects; now exactly 1. Also: seed keyed on `loaded_count` so a corrupt first path can't leave the blank startup project bound, and both restore paths dropped a redundant second `_apply_theme`.
- **B3.2** `browser._stat_cache` (source_path -> (mtime, size), project-independent) survives rebinds instead of forcing a 67k-file re-stat storm on the next stat-based sort.
- **B3.3** FolderBrowser auto-expand: target memoized, expand deferred via `QTimer.singleShot(0)`, `DontWatchForChanges` on the QFileSystemModel.
- **B3.4** ThumbCache rebind path pays zero GUI-thread sqlite: lazy DiskCache connection, pending-writes counters make clean `save_index` a no-op, shared-cache rebind delegates the flush to the worker via a sentinel.
- **B3.5** `_refresh_grid` full-asset scans (star/tag counts + dup-group/variant/used-tag indexes) cached by `(id(project), project.version)`. Rode along: star/tag/tray/tagpanel/dup-variant mutation paths never called `mark_mutated()`, so the version-keyed `_filter_cache` could already serve stale results (star an asset while the Starred filter is active). All sites now bump the version.
- **B3.6** GlobalCacheIndex bounded: ts-stamped rows, oldest evicted past 500k rows (to 400k), checked every 50th worker-side save; legacy schema migrates in place.

### Left open (by design)
- apply_theme stylesheet cache: deferred per plan - the rebind-count fixes remove the repeated applies; reopen only if perf.log still shows tab-switch pain.
- "Remaining GUI-thread I/O" sweep (health panel scan, PSD loads in timeline/composer/platforms): independent modules, kept as the one open Batch 3 item.

### Verification
- New tests: rebind counts per tab op + collection restore, stat-cache survival + reuse, auto-expand memo/defer, DiskCache laziness + no-op commits, scan-cache keying + mark_mutated coverage, index eviction + legacy migration.
- Full suite + `run.py --smoke` green (see final commit).
- Real-world check for the user: startup with a collection, tab switch, By Folder + Newest sort on the 70k project - perf.log should show `rebind_project` / `apply_theme` / `refresh_grid` drops.

author: shepherdjerred
body:
## Why main is red

Buildkite build [5069](https://buildkite.com/sjerred/monorepo/builds/5069) (commit `ecd57aa74`) failed. Classifying the failed jobs by whether they actually block the build (`soft_failed` flag):

| Job | `soft_failed` | Blocks build? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:scissors: Knip` | `true` | No (advisory) |
| `:shield: Trivy Scan` | `true` | No (advisory) |
| `:ship: Deploy scout-for-lol … (prod)` | `false` | **Yes** |
| `:ship: Deploy scout-for-lol … (beta)` | `false` | **Yes** |

The **only hard failure turning main red is the scout-for-lol deploy.** (Build 5063 was marked `passed` overall even though its Knip job had already failed — soft-fail jobs don't fail the build.)

## Root cause

The deploy's `astro build` crashed in the `astro:build:done` OG-image hook:

```
[astro-opengraph-images] jsxDEV_7x81h0kn is not a function
  at ogTemplate (…/frontend/src/lib/og-template.tsx:35:9)
```

`packages/scout-for-lol/packages/frontend/astro.config.mjs` imports `ogTemplate` directly from a raw `.tsx` file. Astro's config loader transpiles that TSX via esbuild; in CI's `oven/bun:1.3.14` (linux x64 **baseline**) container it selects the **dev** automatic JSX runtime and emits `jsxDEV(...)` calls whose `react/jsx-dev-runtime` import gets stripped from the config bundle — leaving `jsxDEV` undefined.

It never surfaced before because OG generation only runs in the **deploy** step (main-only), so PR CI never exercised it; build 5069 was the first completed main build after #1382. It also doesn't reproduce on local mac builds (production runtime is selected there) — it's specific to the CI container's transpile path. The package's presets used by `sjer.red` work because they're pre-compiled to `dist/` by `tsc`; only scout ships a raw-source `.tsx` template imported into the config.

## Fix

Pin `og-template.tsx` to the **classic** JSX runtime via esbuild pragmas so JSX compiles to `React.createElement` (React is already imported and always resolves), independent of the ambient transpile mode:

```tsx
/** @jsxRuntime classic */
/** @jsx React.createElement */
/** @jsxFrag React.Fragment */
import React from "react";
```

## Verification

- Local `astro build` → 43 OG PNGs generated; ESLint + Prettier clean.
- Proved the pragma overrides forced `--jsx=automatic --jsx-dev` (emits `React.createElement`, not `jsxDEV`) **inside the exact CI base image** `oven/bun:1.3.14` (linux x64) — the environment where the failure occurs.

## Out of scope (soft-fail advisories, not fixed here)

Both are non-blocking and were already red on the last `passed` build (5063):

- **Trivy** — ~60 HIGH `CVE-2026-*` findings across ~20 `bun.lock` files + Go modules, repo-wide. Renovate-scale dependency refresh, not a "make CI green" change.
- **Knip** — findings are identical between builds 5063 and 5069; pre-existing advisory noise.

body:
## What & why

Releasing `cobalt-grinding` and `cogrind-workshop` into the new ParkviewLab PyPI org surfaced a handful of general conventions and gotchas that were missing or misleading in the handbook. One of them (a stale local `develop`) nearly shipped a wrong-commit release. Five additive edits across three docs; no structural change; no `VERSION.txt` change (version-guard passes).

## Changes

- **`repo-layout.md` — branch upstream tracking.** The "Creating the layout" sequence set the fetch refspec but never the per-branch upstream, so argument-less `git pull --ff-only` (used throughout the release/back-merge flow) failed with *"no tracking information."* Added the two `--set-upstream-to` lines and a why-note.
- **`releases.md` — sync `develop` before promoting.** `git merge --no-ff develop` merges the *local* worktree; after a GitHub squash-merge that worktree is stale, so the release tags a commit missing the merged work. Added the `git -C ../<repo>-develop pull --ff-only` step and a caution callout.
- **`ci.md` — Org-owned trusted publishers (new convention).** New package → org-level *pending* publisher so it is born org-owned; existing package → org Projects page "Transfer existing project" (not the org→org "Transfer project"); publishers survive the transfer.
- **`ci.md` — TestPyPI dev-release clarification.** Replaced "set up like the PyPI one" with the real differences: workflow `dev-release.yml`, environment `testpypi`, separate instance/account.
- **`releases.md` + `ci.md` — CLI/library "no GHCR".** A pure CLI/library package drops the `docker` job from both `release.yml` and `dev-release.yml`, alongside the existing Electron divergence note.

## Verification

- `reuse lint` — compliant (58/58).
- No `VERSION.txt` change — `version-guard` passes.
- New anchors resolve (`ci.md#org-owned-trusted-publishers`, `repo-layout.md#creating-the-layout`).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Merge is the maintainer's call. A version bump + release is gated separately; on the strength of the new convention (org-owned publishers) the significance is a **minor** bump (`0.9.0 → 0.10.0`).

author: qwesl1123
body:
The control-lock slot was only released in the Socket.IO disconnect
handler, and waiting clients only retried their claim on their own
connect/reconnect. That left two gaps: closing/navigating away from
the page didn't proactively free the slot, and even once released,
other tabs had no way to learn about it short of their own reconnect.

- Add POST /control/release, called via fetch(keepalive) from
  pagehide/beforeunload, mirroring the existing WebRTC/camera cleanup
  pattern.
- Broadcast a control_available event whenever the slot is actually
  freed (clean release or disconnect), and have clients retry
  control_claim when they hear it.
- Tighten Engine.IO ping settings so an unclean disconnect (crash,
  wifi drop, phone backgrounded) is detected in ~15s instead of up to
  ~45s.

author: yegor256
body:
Fixes #426.

## What

`Pgtk::Stash` had no way to tell it that a specific table is too write-heavy to be worth caching. For a high-write, high-parameter-cardinality table (e.g. `invocation` in the issue), every write marks all its cached entries stale at once, the refiller never catches up, and the cache yields zero hit benefit while still burning memory and background DB queries.

## Changes

- **New constructor parameter `volatile:`** (defaults to `[]`) — a list of table names that must never be cached.
- **New bypass branch in `exec`**, beside the existing `pg_*()` one: when the query's read-set intersects `volatile`, the query goes straight to `@pool.exec`. The read-set is computed with `pure.scan(READS_RE)` (FROM/JOIN targets) rather than a raw substring match, so a table name appearing inside a string literal or a column name does **not** falsely disable caching (cf #388).
- **Propagation** of `volatile` to the sub-stash built in `transaction` and `session`, so the bypass holds inside transactions and sessions too.
- Bumped `Metrics/ClassLength` max (from 341 to 343) to accommodate the two new body lines.

`Array#intersect?` (Ruby >= 3.2) is used for the check.

## Tests

Added five tests in `test/test_stash.rb`:
- a volatile table is never cached;
- a non-volatile table is still cached when an unrelated table is volatile;
- the volatile name inside a string literal does not disable caching;
- the bypass propagates into `transaction`;
- the bypass propagates into `session`.

Note: the DB-backed test suite could not be executed in the CI sandbox used here because it requires IPv6 loopback to boot PostgreSQL (`Errno::EAFNOSUPPORT` from `random-port`), which fails for the pre-existing tests too. RuboCop passes cleanly, and the read-set/`intersect?` logic was verified standalone.

author: knoapp
body:
## Description

Companion radios can only hold a bounded number of contacts (a few hundred),
which makes it impossible to track larger populations such as every repeater in
an area. This PR solves that discovery problem entirely client-side by caching
the metadata from adverts the radio hears and persisting it in the browser, so
those nodes stay usable across reloads and reconnects without ever occupying a
slot in the radio's contact table.

The cache is stored **per-radio and encrypted at rest** — the same AES-256-GCM
scheme as message history, under a key derived from the connected radio's own
secrets. Nothing is ever written to the radio itself; a different radio simply
unlocks a different cache.

Changes:

- **Advert cache model** — `lib/map/advertCache.ts` holds the pure merge logic:
  it upserts freshly heard adverts (a re-advert refreshes the stored
  name/type/location, and a known location is never overwritten by an advert
  that arrived without one) and caps the entry count, evicting the
  least-recently-heard nodes.
- **Encrypted per-radio persistence** — `lib/storage.ts` gains
  `saveAdvertCache`/`loadAdvertCache`, storing the cache in its own namespaced
  IndexedDB record encrypted under the per-radio key from `deriveStorageKey`.
  `useMeshCore` loads and merge-restores it on connect (persisted cache under any
  adverts already heard during sync), writes it back debounced on every change,
  and flushes on disconnect/reconnect. The store slice starts empty and is
  scoped to the connected radio.
- **Map** — cached adverts are plotted alongside contacts with slightly faded,
  semi-transparent markers to distinguish discovered nodes from radio-backed
  contacts. Clicking a cached marker opens a read-only detail popup (type,
  public key, last advert, location, distance) with an **Add contact** action
  that saves it to the radio.

author: heyyysandyyy
body:
Summary

Closes #113. Final phase of UX-020 — inner shadow, the one criterion phases 1-2 deferred as needing "real raster compositing, not just another clone." Drop shadow and outer glow both work by giving a real fabric object a native shadow (the host itself, or a clone when a second effect is needed); that trick is fundamentally unavailable for inner shadow, since canvas 2D shadows are physically incapable of casting inward — a shadow always paints outside the casting shape's own pixels, never inside it.

Approach

Real pixel compositing, not a shortcut:
1. Render the host's own silhouette (solid opaque fill, no stroke) at its native local size plus padding for the blur to spread into.
2. Fill a same-size canvas with the shadow colour, punch a hole in it with `destination-out` using the silhouette shifted by the effect's (x, y) offset — this leaves colour visible only in the crescent the shifted copy doesn't cover, on the side opposite the offset (matching CSS's own `inset` shadow convention: offset (4, 4) leaves colour visible on the top/left).
3. Clip that crescent back down to the host's own unshifted silhouette with `destination-in`, so nothing spills outside the shape.
4. Blur it, then clip to the silhouette a second time (blurring spreads colour past the original edge).

Wrapped as a real fabric.Image positioned exactly over the host and inserted above it (inner shadows render on top of the fill, unlike outer effects which sit behind), built from a canvas element directly rather than a data URL — same synchronous canvas-source construction already used elsewhere in this app, which also means it's actually testable (a real image resource load hangs in a test environment that can't decode image bytes; a canvas-element source doesn't need to "load" anything).

An object can now have all three effects active at once. setShadowEffect separates outer effects (drop/glow, which compete for the host's single native shadow slot) from inner (never eligible for that slot regardless of array position) via an explicit rank-based sort plus a filter/find split, rather than relying on array-position assumptions that would silently break once a third kind existed.

Changes
- utils.ts: ShadowEffect's `kind` gains `'inner'`; added INNER_SHADOW_DEFAULT (X/Y/Blur/Color, no spread — matching the original UX-011 acceptance criteria for this kind, opacity folds into colour's alpha like the other two already do).
- effectsEngine.ts: new renderSilhouette/buildInnerShadowTexture/syncInnerShadow/removeInnerShadow, tagged with a new effectRole ('outer'/'inner') alongside the existing effectHostId/effectSlot tags so an inner-shadow edit doesn't tear down unrelated outer-effect clones and vice versa. repositionEffectClones now branches on effectRole — the inner overlay is always positioned by centre (its texture is padded symmetrically around the host), unlike outer clones which copy the host's own origin.
- storage.ts: added effectRole to EXTRA_PROPS proactively, rather than waiting to hit the same undo/reload data-loss bug that hit effectHostId/effectSlot before this (fixed separately in #142).
- objectsSlice.ts: setShadowEffect splits outer vs. inner effects before deciding what goes on the host's native shadow vs. syncEffectClones vs. syncInnerShadow.
- components/CanvasStage.tsx: the object:modified full-rebuild listener now also calls syncInnerShadow; object:removed cleanup now calls a new removeAllEffectVisuals (removeEffectClones deliberately excludes the inner overlay now, so host-deletion cleanup needs the broader one).
- components/EffectsPanel.tsx: added the "Inner shadow" toggle + X/Y/Blur/Colour controls.

Found and fixed during implementation
- renderSilhouette called sc.dispose() before returning the canvas element it had just rendered into — dispose() clears the canvas's own content in place, so every pixel-level test failed with a fully blank texture despite structurally-correct compositing logic elsewhere. Caught by dumping intermediate canvas state rather than trusting the composite math alone; fixed by not disposing (nothing else references the StaticCanvas once the function returns).
- repositionEffectClones originally assumed every tracked effect visual shares the host's own origin convention (true for outer clones). The inner-shadow overlay doesn't — fixed by branching on effectRole. Verified live that rotating via the Properties Panel (the exact path that broke outer effects in an earlier, separate bug) keeps the inner shadow correctly attached.

Test plan
- npx tsc -b --force, npm run lint, npm run build - all pass
- npm test -- run - 132 of 132 passing. effectsEngine.test.ts's new inner-shadow section (7 tests) includes a pixel-level correctness test: for a positive x/y offset, shadow colour is confirmed present near the top-left inside edge and absent near the bottom-right, matching CSS's own inset-shadow convention, not just checking that "some object got created."
- Manually verified end-to-end in a real Chromium browser: toggled inner shadow on a shape, confirmed the visual halo appears on the correct (offset-opposite) side with correct blur falloff; confirmed the overlay is excluded from the layers panel; rotated via the Properties Panel and confirmed the shadow stays attached and correctly rotated; moved the object then pressed Cmd+Z and confirmed the inner shadow survives the undo (the EXTRA_PROPS fix applied proactively here).

Review

Reviewed locally against the project's architecture/security checklist - clean, no issues found.

body:
## Summary

**Risk:** Low–Medium (requires attacker TUI access; defense-in-depth)

**Size:** XS (~74 lines, 1 file)

**Module:** runtime:tools:shell

### What

Adds `TUI_BLOCKED_ENV_VARS`, a static deny-list of environment variables that are **never** forwarded from a TUI client's captured environment to a shell subprocess. When a blocked var is encountered, it is silently skipped (WARN-level log).

### Why

The shell tool's `tui_env` overlay injects every key-value pair from the TUI client after `cmd.env_clear()`, bypassing the `SAFE_ENV_VARS` allowlist (by design — SSH_AUTH_SOCK etc. need to reach subprocesses). However, this means an attacker who compromises or relays the TUI connection can inject library-preload or code-execution variables into the subprocess:

- `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_AUDIT`, `LD_DEBUG` — Unix dynamic-linker injection
- `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH` — macOS equivalent
- `PYTHONPATH`, `PERL5LIB`, `RUBYLIB`, `RUBYOPT` — interpreter code injection
- `IFS`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV` — shell subversion
- `GCONV_PATH`, `LOCPATH`, `COR_PROFILER_PATH` — various library search paths

This is Finding #3 from `docs/maintainers/audits/audit-zeroclaw-2026-07-03.md`.

### Non-goals

- This does **not** change the default allowlist behavior for non-dangerous vars. `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, custom tool paths, etc. still reach the subprocess via TUI as before.
- This does **not** add a configurable audit trail for blocked vars beyond the WARN log.

### Validation evidence

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime -- shell_tui_env` — 5 passed, 0 failed:

  1. `shell_tui_env_is_passed_to_subprocess` — unchanged
  2. `shell_tui_env_overrides_safe_var` — unchanged
  3. `shell_tui_env_none_behaves_like_existing` — unchanged
  4. `shell_tui_env_secrets_reach_subprocess_but_not_safe_list` — unchanged (SSH_AUTH_SOCK still passes)
  5. `shell_tui_env_blocks_dangerous_vars` — **new**: confirms LD_PRELOAD is blocked while SSH_AUTH_SOCK from same TUI is allowed

### Security impact

Positive — closes a defense-in-depth gap in the TUI-to-subprocess env forwarding path.

### Compatibility

Fully backward-compatible. Only env vars on the deny-list are affected; no existing deployment should set any of these vars via TUI in normal operation.

### Rollback

Revert single commit.

### Related

- Audit: `docs/maintainers/audits/audit-zeroclaw-2026-07-03.md` (Finding #3)
- Precedent: `SAFE_ENV_VARS` in the same file provides the existing allowlist pattern

# Add native support for the Quatfit1 multimodal architecture

## Summary

This pull request adds native support for **Quatfit1**, a multimodal architecture derived from Gemma4, to the Transformers library.

Quatfit1 introduces a dedicated `model_type` (`quatfit1`) while leveraging the existing Gemma4 implementation. Native integration allows Quatfit models to be loaded directly through the Transformers Auto Classes without requiring `trust_remote_code=True`.

---

## Motivation

Currently, Quatfit models require remote code execution to be loaded:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
```

With native Transformers support, users can simply write:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    "Quatfit/Quatfit-Mini"
)
```

---

## Features

Quatfit1 supports:

- Text generation
- Image understanding
- Audio understanding
- Video understanding
- Multimodal instruction following
- Long-context inference
- Hugging Face Auto Classes

---

## Architecture

Quatfit1 is implemented as a Gemma4-derived architecture with full configuration, modeling, feature extraction, image processing, video processing, and processor classes.

The following configuration classes are introduced:

- `Quatfit1Config` (`model_type = "quatfit1"`)

- `Quatfit1Processor`

- `Quatfit1ImageProcessor`

- `Quatfit1VideoProcessor`

A weight conversion script is also included:

## Summary

Two behavior-preserving refactors of the generator internals, each pinned by the 94 macro-expansion tests (379 tests total pass unchanged).

### Split `eraseGenericTypes` into per-category helpers

`eraseGenericTypes(in:genericParamNames:)` was a single ~130-line function mixing two concerns: categories that must run even for non-generic declarations (stripping `@escaping`, unwrapping single-element tuples, rewriting `T!` to `T?`, erasing typed-throws clauses inside function types) and categories that only substitute generic parameters. It is now an ordered dispatcher delegating to one helper per type category:

- Always run: `eraseAttributedType`, `eraseTupleType`, `eraseImplicitlyUnwrappedOptionalType`, `eraseFunctionType`.
- After the `genericParamNames.isEmpty` short-circuit: `eraseIdentifierType`, `eraseOptionalType`, `eraseArrayType`.

The dispatch order preserves the original precedence exactly; the "runs even when non-generic" contract is now stated once at the dispatcher instead of repeated as an inline comment on each branch. Helpers that leave a type unchanged return `nil` so the dispatcher falls through to the final `return type`, matching the previous fall-through semantics.

### Share the reset-target enumeration between the two reset methods

`generateRegularResetMethod` and `generateSendableResetMethod` each walked the requirements and rebuilt the same list of `<member> = <value>` resets (call count → `0`, call args → `[]`, handler/backing → `nil`), differing only in the storage prefix (`Self.`/none vs `storage.`) and one edge case. That enumeration now lives in a single `resetTargets(for:methodGroups:lockBased:)` returning `ResetTarget` values; each method applies its own prefix. The one genuine difference — get-set variables reset `_name` backing storage under a lock but reset optional properties directly otherwise — is captured by the `lockBased` flag.

### Deliberately not included

The three `#if`-preserving mappers (`mapMemberBlockItemsPreservingIfConfig` / `mapCodeBlockItemsPreservingIfConfig` / `mapLinesPreservingIfConfig`) were left as-is. ## Summary

Largo (the AI terminal) has 4 overlapping flow-related tools whose descriptions gave Claude almost nothing to disambiguate against each other — and one description was factually stale. This PR rewrites all 4 to the `get_ecosystem_context`/`get_spx_play` quality bar (task #110/#123 precedent), and fixes a real routing-hint gap found while auditing the intent regex per the task's explicit ask.

Full write-up: `docs/audit/FINDINGS.md`, new entry right after the intro `---` (title: "4 overlapping Largo flow tools had thin, non-disambiguating descriptions, one of them factually stale; a real routing-regex gap silently dropped 3 of the 4 from Largo's tool allowlist for common phrasing").

## Root cause — description quality

1. **`get_postgres_flows`** and **`get_flow_tape`** call, respectively, `marketPlatform.flows.getFlowTape()` and `marketPlatform.flows.getFlowTapeSummary()` (`src/lib/platform/flow-service.ts`). `getFlowTapeSummary()`'s own body is `const rows = await getFlowTape(opts); ... return { count, total_premium, top_tickers, recent: rows }` — so `get_flow_tape` is a strict **superset** of `get_postgres_flows`: identical Postgres rows, returned verbatim as `get_flow_tape`'s own `recent` field, plus aggregates on top. Neither description said so.
2. **`get_options_flow`**'s description read *"UW ONLY — live flow alerts, 0DTE premium, strike_stacks... No Polygon equivalent."* — but `run-tool.ts`'s case (line 485) explicitly merges up to 48h/500 rows of HELIX's Postgres-ingested tape (`fetchRecentFlows`) into the non-SPX-ticker branch, dedupes it against a live UW pull, computes `strike_stacks` over the merged set, and reports `helix_session_alerts` + `source: "unusual_whales + helix"` in the very same response the description claims is pure UW. "No Polygon equivalent" is still true (Polygon has no flow-alerts product at all); "UW ONLY" was not.
3. **`get_global_flow`** had no stated relationship to the other 3 — it's actually the *one* tool of the four that's genuinely pure live UW REST with zero Postgres/HELIX involvement (confirmed: `run-tool.ts` line 1243 → `fetchUwGlobalFlowAlerts()` → a single `/api/option-trades/flow-alerts` pull, nothing else).

## Root cause — routing regex (task's ask #3)

Investigated `FLOW_RE`/`FLOW_TOOLS_RE` for a task #110/#127-style ambiguity between these 4 tools, and found something more concrete: the regex already lists `sweep`/`sweeps` as siblings, but had **no sibling for `flow` itself** — `\bflow\b` doesn't match "flows" (plural) or "flowing" (gerund). Verified with a standalone repro calling `getToolsForIntent`/`analyzeLargoQuestion` directly: for a ticker-less question like *"any options flows building up today"*, `needsFlow` came back `false` and **`get_options_flow`/`get_global_flow`/`get_postgres_flows` were completely absent from `getToolsForIntent`'s return value** — not a soft-hint miss, an actually-unreachable-tool bug. This same regex also gates a real pre-fetch in `largo-live-feed.ts` (`if (intent.needsFlow) { tool("get_flow_tape", ...); tool("get_greek_flow", ...); }`), so it wasn't just a text-quality issue.

Fixed by adding `flows`/`flowing` as explicit alternatives, matching the file's own existing `sweep`/`sweeps` style — not a new regex idiom. Deliberately did **not** chase `outflow(s)`/`inflow(s)` (compound words, no word boundary before "flow" at all — a structurally different fix, and `get_etf_flow`/`get_sector_flow` vocabulary, not one of this task's 4 tools); documented as a known follow-up in FINDINGS.md instead of scope-creeping this PR.

**Aside, explicitly NOT fixed here:** while isolating the regex bug from ticker-mention noise, found `KNOWN_TICKERS` contains short tickers that collide with common English words (e.g. `"NOW"` = ServiceNow, matching any question ending "...right now"). Pre-existing, platform-wide, out of scope for this task — flagged in FINDINGS.md for a future pass.

## Fix

- Rewrote all 4 descriptions (`src/lib/largo/tool-defs.ts`) to state exactly what fields come back, exactly which data source produced them, and to explicitly name/disambiguate against the other 3 by tool name.
- Widened `FLOW_RE`/`FLOW_TOOLS_RE` (`src/lib/largo/intent-keywords.ts`) to add `flows`/`flowing`.
- `get_postgres_flows`'s schema gained `default: 25` on `limit` — documents (doesn't change) its existing `run-tool.ts` runtime default.

**No behavior/data change:** `run-tool.ts` is untouched (`git diff main -- src/lib/largo/run-tool.ts` is empty) — this is a documentation/routing-hint fix only, per the task's explicit constraint. `git diff main -- src/lib/spx-signals.ts` is also empty.

## Blast radius

The `FLOW_RE` widening is also read by every other tool bundled into `TOOL_GROUPS.flow_analysis`/`TOOL_GROUPS.spx_desk` (`get_dark_pool`, `get_nope`, `get_flow_per_strike`, `get_greek_flow`, etc.) — all of them now also correctly become reachable for "flows"/"flowing" phrasing. This is a strict widening: every previously-matching alternative is untouched, so nothing that was reachable before became unreachable.

## Tests

- `src/lib/largo/tool-defs.test.ts` (+7): stale UW-only claim replaced with an accurate, testable HELIX-merge description; all 4 descriptions cross-reference each other by name; superset relationship documented both directions; `strike_stacks` presence/absence documented correctly; `getToolsForIntent` allowlist regression test for the regex fix.
- `src/lib/largo/question-intent.test.ts` (+2): `needsFlow` now fires for "flows"/"flowing"; bare singular "flow" still fires (no regression).

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (Node 22).
- Full suite **1177/1177 passing on Node 22** (33 pre-existing, unrelated failures reproduced identically on a clean `main` via `git stash`/`git stash pop` — documented Node 22 vs. CI's Node 20 divergence).

author: maccman
body:
## Problem

Task View deliberately keeps a session-only middle state: a task completed there stays visible, struck through, until you archive it (V1's workflow, with a quick undo path). A support report exposed the missing reconciliation path: if the same checkbox is flipped back to `[ ]` in the source note (e.g. a daily note), the index reports the task open again — but the session's `[x]` copy kept shadowing the real open row. The row kept offering **Reopen**, and clicking it tried to locate the old `[x]` line in markdown that had already changed, producing the "task line no longer in note" toast.

## Change

The struck set now yields to the index when they disagree, using `updatedAt` (the note's indexed mtime, epoch ms) to tell a genuine reopen apart from a stale read:

- **`reconcileRecentlyCompleted(root, open)`** (`apps/desktop/src/lib/tasks/recently-completed.ts`): a live open row with the same task key and a **strictly newer** `updatedAt` means the note was rewritten and reindexed since the completion — the struck shadow is dropped and the live row shows.
- An open row with an **unchanged** `updatedAt` is the pre-completion index state — a refetch racing the completion's reindex — and keeps its shadow, preserving the existing guarantee that a just-checked row can't flicker back to open (`tasks-screen.test.tsx` covers both directions).
- `useRecentlyCompleted(root)` → `useRecentlyCompleted(root, open)`: the hook reconciles against the open query's data internally, so the desktop screen and the mobile Tasks tab get the fix through the one shared path and future surfaces can't skip it.
- The reconciliation applies at two layers (second commit, after a Bugbot finding): the returned view filters superseded rows **during render** — the very first render that sees the fresh open data shows the live row, leaving no frame where the stale shadow could still offer a doomed Reopen — while an effect prunes the store singleton so `hasRecentlyCompleted` and the Archive count agree immediately after. Both layers share one pure core (`withoutReopened`).

No write-path changes; this is purely view-state reconciliation. The completed-on-disk `[x]` history behind "show archived" is untouched.

## Why `updatedAt` is the right discriminator

`notes.updated_at` is stamped from the file's mtime on every reindex (`apply_note` in `src-tauri/src/db/write.rs`). A reopened task can only reappear in the open read after its note was rewritten and reindexed, so its row necessarily carries a newer `updatedAt` than the copy captured at completion time. The stale-refetch race returns the pre-completion row with the original `updatedAt`, so strict `>` separates the two cases exactly.

## Testing

- New unit tests for `reconcileRecentlyCompleted` (drop on newer `updatedAt`, hold on equal, graph-root scoping, hook-level reconcile + store prune agreement).
- A render-phase capture test proves the superseded shadow is excluded in the same render that sees the fresh open data, before any effect runs.
- New `TasksScreen` integration tests: external reopen sheds the struck row and offers **Complete** again; a refetch racing the completion's reindex keeps the row struck.
- `pnpm check` (typecheck + oxlint + eslint) clean; full task + mobile suites pass (36 files, 345 tests).

## Risk

Low. The reconcile only ever *removes* entries from the ephemeral session set, and only when the index reports the task open with a newer note mtime. Worst case on a pathological mtime tie (sub-millisecond complete-then-reopen) is the current behavior, not a new failure.

Closes #1262

## Problem

`Moq1100` (callback signature should match mocked method) raised a false positive when a callback lambda parameter used a multi-token ref modifier list such as `scoped ref` or `ref readonly`. The private `GetRefKind` helper inspected only `parameter.Modifiers[0]`, so `scoped ref string` resolved to `scoped` -> `RefKind.None`, which no longer matched the mocked method's `RefKind.Ref`.

## Fix

Use the already-resolved `parameterSymbol.RefKind` (the authoritative semantic ref kind) instead of re-deriving it from the first syntax token. Removed the now-dead `GetRefKind` helper. Symbol-to-symbol `RefKind` comparison needs no mapping and handles every modifier combination (`ref`, `in`, `out`, `ref readonly`, `scoped ref`).

- Positive: `(scoped ref string data) => {}` against `DoRef(ref string)` -> no diagnostic.
- Negative: `(scoped ref DateTime timestamp) => {}` against `DoIn(in DateTime)` -> still `Moq1100` (ref != in).

Covers positive, negative, and the boundary modifier-token case.

The `deploy-testflight` job failed at `.app` signing because `MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_BASE64` contains only a `3rd Party Mac Developer Installer` cert — which is correctly excluded from `CODE_IDENTITY` (installer certs can't sign `.app` bundles) — leaving `CODE_ID` empty and causing `codesign` to error with `no identity found`.

## Changes

  - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-keychain
    id: mac-keychain
    with:
      cert_base64:   ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_BASE64 }}
      cert_password: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_PASSWORD }}
      cert_base64_2:   ${{ secrets.MACOS_APP_CERT_BASE64 }}    # new

body:
## Summary

Replaces the public booking availability query with a tenant-scoped RPC.

The previous `public.public_appointment_slots` view used `security_invoker = true`. Because `anon` correctly has no `SELECT` privilege on `public.appointments`, public booking requests failed with:

```txt
permission denied for table appointments
```

This PR moves public slot lookup to a dedicated `security definer` function without exposing the appointments table.

## What changed

* Adds `public.get_public_appointment_slots(uuid)`
* Requires an explicit `barbershop_id`
* Uses a restricted `search_path`
* Returns only non-sensitive availability data
* Filters results to the requested tenant
* Filters inactive barbershops and barbers
* Returns only future `scheduled` and `confirmed` appointments
* Updates `appointmentRepository.ts` to use `supabase.rpc`
* Rejects empty tenant IDs before calling Supabase
* Prevents public booking from continuing without a resolved tenant
* Removes direct application reads from `public_appointment_slots`
* Updates unit, integration and E2E tests
* Updates security, deployment and booking documentation

## RPC contract

Input:

```txt
p_barbershop_id uuid
```

Returned fields:

```txt
barber_id
barber_name
start_at
end_at
status
barbershop_id
```

The RPC does not return:

* client name
* client phone
* notes
* service value
* financial data
* internal appointment details

## Security

* No public `SELECT` was granted on `public.appointments`
* No public appointment-read policy was added
* No global slot query is supported
* No default tenant or fixed UUID was introduced
* The function uses qualified `public.*` objects
* The function uses `security definer`
* Execution is granted only to `anon` and `authenticated`
* Existing owner and barber internal appointment reads remain unchanged
* The legacy view is not dropped or revoked in this PR

## Repository changes

`listPublicAppointmentSlots` now:

* requires `barbershopId: string`
* trims and validates the tenant ID
* fails before Supabase when the tenant ID is empty
* calls:

```ts
supabase.rpc('get_public_appointment_slots', {
  p_barbershop_id: scopedBarbershopId
})
```

* preserves the existing appointment-slot mapping
* preserves local fallback behavior for development while filtering by tenant

## Tests

Updated coverage verifies that:

* the repository calls `get_public_appointment_slots`
* the exact `p_barbershop_id` is sent
* the legacy view is no longer queried by the application
* empty tenant IDs are rejected before Supabase
* slot mapping is preserved
* public booking remains tenant-scoped
* E2E mocks the RPC endpoint
* owner and barber internal reads continue using `appointments`

## Validation

```txt
npm run test
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm run validate
npm run check
npm audit --audit-level=moderate
npx playwright test
```

Results:

```txt
Vitest: 19 files, 258 tests passed
Playwright: 15 passed, 2 skipped
TypeScript: passed
Build: passed
Validate: passed
Check: passed
Audit: 0 vulnerabilities
```

## Rollout

The RPC must be applied before the new frontend is published:

1. Review `docs/public-appointment-availability-rpc.sql`
2. Apply the SQL manually in Supabase
3. Confirm `public.get_public_appointment_slots(uuid)`
4. Test the RPC as `anon`
5. Validate the Vercel preview
6. Merge and publish the frontend
7. Confirm `/book/:slug`
8. Evaluate removal of legacy view access in a later change

## Scope

This PR changes only the public booking availability contract, repository integration, tests and related documentation.

It does not change:

* authentication
* owner or barber internal appointment reads
* appointment creation rules
* appointment status logic
* conflict detection
* the unique appointment index
* RLS policies
* package files
* dependencies
* lockfiles
* the remote Supabase database

body:
## 背景 / 問題

記録される合計ワークアウト時間が、**実時間より短く**出ていた（体感報告）。特に「レップ間休憩を少し伸ばそうとポーズ」すると、そのポーズ分がまるごと消える（例: 5分ポーズ → 約5分短い）。

原因は `TimerService.elapsedSecondsNow()` が経過時間からポーズ累積（`totalPausedMillis` / 現在ポーズ中の `currentPauseMillis`）を**意図的に差し引いていた**こと。この値が完了時に `state.elapsedSeconds` → 履歴の `totalSeconds` となり、以下すべての唯一のワークアウト時間として使われる:

- Wear 履歴 / 完了画面
- companion の「合計時間」表示
- **Health Connect のセッション長**（`start = 完了時刻 − totalSeconds`）
- **PDS の duration / 開始時刻**

## 変更

- `elapsedSecondsNow()` を **開始〜現在の実時計**（`(now - startedAtElapsedMillis)/1000`）に簡素化し、ポーズ時間も算入する。
- 不要になったポーズ会計（`pausedAtElapsedMillis` / `totalPausedMillis` / `foldPauseTime()`）を削除。
- 副作用として、Health Connect / PDS のセッション開始時刻が実開始とほぼ一致するようになる（従来はポーズ分後ろにズレていた）。

各フェーズのカウントダウン（`TimerPhase.remainingSeconds`）はポーズ中に凍結される正しい挙動のまま。スナップショット復帰の挙動も不変。「休憩±10秒調整」「無制限休憩」は元々フェーズを実秒で進めるため記録に乗っており、ポーズもそれと同じ扱いになる。

## テスト

- ✅ `:app:testDebugUnitTest` + `:app:lintDebug` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- ⏳ 実機での手動 E2E（本命・レビュー後に確認予定）: ワークアウト中にポーズ→数十秒待つ→再開→完走 して、完了画面/履歴の合計がポーズを含む実経過にほぼ一致することを確認

## メモ

計時は `SystemClock` 依存で決定的なユニットテストが難しいため、ポーズ計時の自動テストは追加していない（クロック注入リファクタが必要でスコープ外）。

body:
Adds an **APRS Activity** window (Tools → APRS Activity) that talks to AetherSDR's KISS-over-TCP TNC (default `127.0.0.1:8001`), decodes the off-air AX.25/APRS traffic, and shows a live roster of heard stations — aimed at the 2 m / 70 cm transverter crew who want a "who's on APRS right now" radar of what their own radio heard off-air.

## What's in it
- **`AprsDecode.{h,cpp}`** — clean-room KISS framing + AX.25 UI decode/encode + APRS position/message parsing. Pure logic, no sockets, unit-testable. **23 unit tests** (`-DSHACKLOG_TESTS=ON`), all passing; canned frames were generated by an independent Python encoder so the C++ decoder is cross-checked against a separate implementation.
- **`AprsKissClient.{h,cpp}`** — `QTcpSocket` KISS/TCP client. Buffers incoming bytes through `kissUnframe` → `decodeAx25`, emits decoded reports; TX path builds UI frames and writes them back as KISS data frames. Auto-reconnects on the same 1/2/5/10/30 s backoff as the existing TCI client.
- **`AprsStationModel.{h,cpp}`** — `QAbstractTableModel` roster deduped by source call-SSID, tracking last-heard / position / comment / packet count, great-circle **distance + bearing** from `MY_GRIDSQUARE` (Maidenhead → lat/lon + haversine), a **✓ against any call already in the log**, and stale-station ageout (default last hour).
- **`AprsActivityDialog.{h,cpp}`** — the window: connection controls, sortable roster table, and a message-send row (the seed for a future mailbox stage). Non-modal, lazily created, mirrors `SectionMapDialog`'s wiring.
- Wired into the Tools menu; `CHANGELOG.md` updated.

License note: ShackLog is MIT. AE's GPL packet decoder was used **only as a correctness reference**, not copied — the decoder here is a fresh implementation from the AX.25 + APRS specs.

## Verification
- **Full app builds clean** (Windows/MSVC, `windeployqt` bundles the runtime); GUI smoke-launches.
- **23 decoder unit tests pass.**
- **RX path live-proven against real AetherSDR**: enabled AE's AetherModem KISS TNC on :8001 with a slice on 145.070 FM (IC-9700 via aether-gate). ShackLog connects; real off-air packet traffic decoded end-to-end (AE's MHeard showed live W3SMD / N5TB position beacons from the same stream).

## Known limitation (not in this code)
The **TX path can't key the radio in the current bench setup** — but the blocker is downstream in the aether-gate bridge, whose `transmit set` handler acknowledges the command and reports "transmitting" back to AE without ever asserting PTT on the rig (documented separately in aether-gate). ShackLog builds and sends a valid frame and AE accepts it; no RF is produced because the gate's TX seam is unwired. When a Flex-native radio or a gate with PTT is used, the same send path should key normally.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- A map view reusing the distance/bearing data.
- Messaging/mailbox stage — note AE already has its own PMS, so that stage should talk to AE's mailbox rather than reimplement one.

author: rodaddy
body:
## Why
Makes `openbrain-memory` redaction a true **superset** of the rtech-hermes vendored fork so that fork can retire (rtech-hermes #92: "use OB, not a fork; if there are issues, fix them in OB"). The fork's B2 parity report found the package UNDER-redacts 4 classes it catches.

## What
Adds two heuristic catch-all detectors ported from the fork:
1. **Bare 3-segment non-JWT token** `x.y.z` (the non-`eyJ` sibling of JWT_LIKE_RE — opaque `token.a.sig` shapes).
2. **Unlabeled 40+ char high-entropy blob containing a symbol** (`- _ + / =`).

**Anti-SHA guard preserved:** the `(?=.*[+/=_-])` symbol-requirement lookahead is load-bearing — a pure-hex git SHA / content hash has no symbol, so it is NOT redacted. This is exactly why the package originally narrowed to `LABELED_LONG_SECRET_RE`; the symbol requirement restores the fork's catch-all coverage without reintroducing SHA over-redaction.

## ⚠️ Design decision the reviewer should scrutinize (not a defect — a deliberate layering)
`SECRET_PATTERNS` has **two** consumers in this package: `redact_text` (cosmetic redaction) AND `agent._reject_secret_payload` (a **fail-closed receipt reject gate**). The fork only ever used these patterns for redaction.

A verbatim add to `SECRET_PATTERNS` broke the reject gate: the high-entropy heuristic matches benign 40+ char slash/underscore **file paths** (a test receipt command path is exactly 40 chars), causing a valid receipt to be **falsely rejected** (`test_record_receipt_routes_to_receipt_session_event` went RED).

**Resolution:** the two heuristics live in a new `HEURISTIC_REDACTION_PATTERNS` list, and `REDACTION_PATTERNS = SECRET_PATTERNS + HEURISTIC_REDACTION_PATTERNS`. `redact_text` (and `redact_value` → `_redact_value` → `redact_text`, and the spool payload path) apply BOTH lists. The fail-closed reject gate keeps using ONLY the high-confidence `SECRET_PATTERNS`.

**The posture this creates (call it out explicitly):** an unlabeled high-entropy secret in a payload is now REDACTED in recall text but still ACCEPTED by the receipt reject gate (written to OB, redacted). This preserves fork parity (the fork redacts, has no reject gate) without importing false rejections into the availability gate. If reviewers think the reject gate SHOULD also fail-closed on these classes, that's a follow-up decision — flagged here deliberately.

## Redaction table (proven at runtime)
| Class | before | after |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| bare 3-seg non-`eyJ` token | clear (LEAK) | **REDACTED** |
| 40+ high-entropy w/ dash | clear (LEAK) | **REDACTED** |
| 40+ high-entropy w/ underscore | clear (LEAK) | **REDACTED** |
| 40+ blob w/ `+/=` base64 | clear (LEAK) | **REDACTED** |
| 40-hex git SHA (negative) | clear | **clear** (guard holds) |
| 64-hex content hash (negative) | clear | **clear** (guard holds) |
| benign 40-char file-path receipt (reject gate) | accepted | **accepted** (gate untouched) |

## Tests + gates
- 6 new tests in `test_safety.py` (4 positive classes + 2 SHA negatives). Runtime-assembled samples, no literal secrets.
- `uv run pytest` → 178 passed, 5 skipped (pre-existing live-canary skips). `ruff check` clean, `mypy` clean, new test format-clean, ggshield clean.

## Critical pass (pre-PR, done)

author: ashigirl96
body:
## 概要

外部の Rust プロセスから稼働中の Monica にセッション作成を依頼すると、常設「sdk」Runspace に新しい Tab が生え、事前 mint した UUID で claude が起動する経路を作る（#306 の MVP2）。

設計は headless-first: セッション作成 + claude 起動（launch コマンドの PTY 注入まで）を backend だけで完結させ、フロントは `SdkSessionOpened` event で作成済みセッションを adopt/attach する観測者に徹する。claude の実起動が webview のライフサイクル（main window の有無・WorkBench の visit 履歴・event の到達）に依存しない。

入口は暫定 Tauri command ではなく **UDS 制御ソケット**（`<base>/sdk.sock`、NDJSON 1 req/res）。`monica-claude-sdk::open_session()` から外部 Rust バイナリで叩ける実入口が今できるため、unused-commands ゲートへの allowlist ハックも不要になった。外部口は「Rust クライアント=UDS / browser=WebSocket（MVP7 #313）」の二面構成（#306/#313 にコメントで明文化済み）。

close #308

## 主な変更

- **外部 Rust バイナリからセッション作成できる**: 新規 leaf crate `monica-sdk-protocol`（NDJSON DTO + version handshake）と `monica-claude-sdk::open_session()` / `examples/open_session.rs` を追加。desktop の `sdk_server`（app setup で起動、接続ごとにスレッド、socket は 0600）が受け付ける
- **セッション作成のトランザクションは application 層が所有**: `ExecutionService::open_sdk_session` が cwd 検証（絶対パス必須）→ claude_session_id / tab_id の uuid 事前 mint → `create_terminal_session`（kind=Agent, runspace="sdk", env に `MONICA_SDK_SESSION_ID`）→ ack 付き launch 注入（`TerminalDaemon::write_input` を port に追加）→ 失敗時は terminate + Failed に rollback → 成功時のみ `SdkSessionOpened` を emit
- **Workbench は作成済みセッションを adopt**: `adoptSdkSessionAtom` が「sdk」runspace を get-or-create し、sessionId 束縛済み Tab を append（既存 attach/replay パスに乗る）。外部トリガーなのでフォーカスは奪わない。event 消失時も reconcile が Detached 群に落とすので手動 reattach 可能（自動回収は MVP3）
- create params: `cwd`（必須・絶対パス）/ `model` / `title`（初期タブタイトル）

## 設計上のポイント

- **runTaskFlow 同型（フロント駆動 materialize）からの反転**: 当初案はフロントが Tab mount 時にセッションを作る形だったが、SDK を名乗る以上 claude 起動を webview に人質に取らせない、という判断で backend 完結に変更。Issue #308 の実装方針も改訂済み
- **launch write は fire-and-forget ではなく ack 付き**: ptyd は接続ごとに別スレッドなので、notify だと `open_session` 直後の `send_text` が launch を追い越して素の shell prompt に落ちる（= prompt が shell コマンドとして実行される）余地があった。daemon の応答を待ってから返す
- **retry 意味論**: server が返すエラー = rollback 済みで retry 安全。transport 障害（応答喪失）= 結果不明で、doc とエラーメッセージで「Workbench を確認してから retry」と誘導。idempotency key は mapping 永続化が前提なので MVP3（#309 にコメント済み）。claude 起動成功の readiness handshake は hook/JSONL シグナルが前提なので MVP4（#310 にコメント済み）
- **CLAUDE_WRAPPER / ptyd プロトコル / use-terminal は無変更**: `--session-id` は claude のネイティブフラグで、SDK セッションは task 外（`MONICA_TASK_ID` 未設定）なので wrapper は素通し。sessionId 束縛済み Tab は runConnect が create せず attach する既存挙動をそのまま使う
- adopt が terminal state 未ロードで走ると捏造 initialState に書き込んで保存済みレイアウトを壊すため、`loadTerminalStateAtom` を先に await する（`createTaskRunspaceAtom` と同じ前例）

## 動作確認

`just test`（cargo workspace + bun 129 tests）/ `bunx tsc --noEmit` / `just check` 全通過。E2E は `just dev` 起動後に実バイナリで確認:

```bash
# アプリ未起動 → 「is the Monica app running?」の明確なエラー
MONICA_HOME=~/monica/dev cargo run -p monica-claude-sdk --example open_session -- --cwd <path>

# アプリ起動後（headless 証明）
MONICA_HOME=~/monica/dev cargo run -p monica-claude-sdk --example open_session -- --cwd <worktree>
# → claude_session_id / session_id / tab_id が返り、claude がフロント操作なしで起動
#   PTY env に MONICA_SDK_SESSION_ID 注入、sdk.sock は srw------- (0600)

MONICA_HOME=~/monica/dev cargo run -p monica-claude-sdk --example send_text -- --tab <tab-id> "reply with just: OK"
# → ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<事前mint UUID>.jsonl が生成（claude は初回メッセージで transcript を遅延生成）
#   Workbench の sdk Runspace の Tab に claude 画面 + 送受信内容が attach/replay で表示
#   claude のステータスバーの Session ID が事前 mint UUID と一致

# 2 回目の open_session（--model sonnet --title sdk-test-2）
# → Runspace は増えず既存「sdk」に 2 個目の Tab（get-or-create）。initial_command に --model 'sonnet'、Tab タイトルに sdk-test-2

# 存在しない cwd → SdkResponse::Err（validation）
```

レビュー: feature-dev:code-reviewer 3 フェーズ（テストカバレッジ / 一般 3 並列 / 依存方向）+ Codex 敵対的レビュー 5 巡の指摘を全て解消または後続 MVP（#309/#310）へ引き継ぎ済み。

author: deano-bravo
body:
Full-solution maintainability pass from a structured review of the codebase (backend, web front end, data layer, tests, build/deploy infra).

## Bug fixes
- **Web app never registered the tenant policies** — `Todos.razor` gates its delete column on `RequireTenantAdmin` via `AuthorizeView`, but only the API called `AddTenantPolicies()`; resolving an unregistered policy throws at render time. The Web composition root now registers the shared policy set.
- **Password policy drift** — the Register form allowed 6-char passwords while the server requires 12; both now read `PasswordPolicy.MinimumLength`.
- **Unguarded signing-key decode** — a malformed `jwt-signing-key` secret crashed with a raw `FormatException`; `ApiJwtDefaults.GetSigningKeyBytes` now fails fast with an actionable message (missing / non-base64 / <32 bytes) on both the minting (Web) and validating (API) sides.
- **Health endpoints were Development-only** while the AppHost wires `WithHttpHealthCheck` and the k8s chart deploys to Production — `/health` and `/alive` are now mapped in all environments (exposure trade-off recorded in CLAUDE.md tech debt).

## Architecture
- New dependency-free **`AspireWeb.Contracts`** project — deletes the DTO copies duplicated between Web and ApiService and replaces the anonymous `new { title }` payload with the typed contract.
- **`TenantProvisioningService`** — the tenant+owner transaction (execution strategy, `ChangeTracker.Clear()`, unique-violation handling, rollback) moves out of `Register.razor` into an injectable, testable service.
- **Shared DbContext registration** (`AddAppDbContext` / `AddIdentityDbContext` in `AspireWeb.Data`) replaces three near-identical blocks and owns the Identity schema-version pin.
- **API consistency** — weather endpoint extracted to an `Endpoints/` module; todos endpoints gain max-length validation (400 instead of a 500 via `DbUpdateException`), RFC 7807 responses for every non-2xx, OpenAPI metadata, a list cap, and centralized normalization (`TodoItem.NormalizeTitle`).
- **Honest client errors** — `TodoApiClient` returns a `TodoWriteOutcome` so the UI distinguishes duplicate / forbidden / not-found / server-fault instead of labeling every failure as a permissions problem; `CancellationToken` plumbed through token minting.
- **Constants consolidated** — `Tenants` table name, Identity schema version (3 copies), security-stamp interval (2 manually-synced copies), API service URL.
- **Index convention fix** — the tenant-filter convention no longer adds a single-column `TenantId` index when a composite index already leads on it; `DropRedundantTodoTenantIndex` migration removes `IX_TodoItems_TenantId`.
- `ActiveTenantGate` caches inactive verdicts for 5s (was 60s), so reactivated tenants are unblocked promptly.

## Tests & CI
- `AppFixture` converted from an assembly fixture to a **collection fixture** (xunit.v3 creates assembly fixtures eagerly, so trait filtering alone would still boot Docker) + `Category=Integration` traits → a genuine Docker-free fast tier that runs in seconds.
- `dotnet test` moves to the **Microsoft.Testing.Platform** runner (`global.json` `test` section); the no-op `coverlet.collector` is replaced by `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` 17.14.x (18.x requires MTP v2, unsupported by xunit.v3 3.2.2 — pinned with a comment).
- **New tests**: `TenantTokenServiceTests` (9 cases) validates minted tokens against the exact parameters the API enforces — killing the drift risk with the test-only `MintJwt`; `TodoEndpointTests` covers the previously untested 400/409/204/404 paths.
- **Two-tier GitHub Actions CI**: build `-warnaserror` + fast tests with coverage artifact, then the AppHost integration suite (Docker preinstalled on ubuntu-latest; DCP ships via Aspire NuGet).

## Docs & hygiene
Deploy recipe consolidated into `.claude/commands/deploy-k8s.md` (CLAUDE.md now points there); README rewritten with tiered test commands and a CI badge; MIT `LICENSE` added; stale `gen-cert.ps1` reference fixed; CLAUDE.md updated (Contracts project, conventions, MTP commands, CI section, new tech-debt entries).

## Verification
- `dotnet build AspireWeb.slnx -c Release -warnaserror --no-incremental` — clean.
- Fast tier (`--filter-not-trait Category=Integration`): 14 tests in ~8s, no AppHost/Docker boot.
- Full suite: **24/24 passed** through the real AppHost (Postgres container + both migration chains, including the new index-drop migration).
- Still worth a manual once-over: `aspire run` → register two orgs → confirm the delete column renders for owners without the Blazor error UI (the fixed bug), and a Production-environment `/health` probe.

author: tony71200
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce frequent commits and avoid SQLite contention by batching face/person DB writes during scan and clustering. 
- Improve recluster UX by exposing real-time status, logs and a stop request button in the UI. 
- Prevent very long or multiline messages from cluttering recluster logs.

### Description
- Set SQLite pragmas in `db.get_conn()` to `busy_timeout=5000` and `journal_mode=WAL` for better concurrency. 
- Add optional `commit` flags to `add_face`, `create_person`, and `set_face_person` and implement `add_faces_batch` and `set_faces_person_batch` helpers in `backend/db.py` to support batch transactions. 
- Use `add_faces_batch` in `backend/main.py` scan flow to insert faces in a single transaction. 
- In `backend/clustering.py`, defer per-row commits during incremental clustering by calling DB functions with `commit=False` and perform a single `conn.commit()` at the end with rollback-on-exception. 
- Adjust `split_face_to_new_person` to create the person without committing immediately so the following assignment can be part of the same transaction. 
- Replace `_append_recluster_log` with `_recluster_log` in `backend/main.py` to sanitize and truncate messages, and update all recluster log calls accordingly. 
- Frontend changes: add a wider recluster modal with status panel, counters and a logs textarea, add polling and stop-request logic (`/recluster/status`, `/recluster/cancel`), wire UI buttons, add translations for the stop button, and include CSS styling for the new panel.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.
